The text reads: "re-deriving it today (`resolve_reviewable_head` from this branch's tip) resolves to `7da6f47` -- a commit that modifies `HANDOFF.md` ... So this PR is not currently a live instance: its green `lwb-lanes` does attest to review of `7da6f47`'s content."

PROVENANCE, which is what makes this a defect rather than ordinary drift. `git log -S'7da6f47' -- reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md` returns exactly one commit: a147d1d, the second-to-last commit on this branch, whose own subject is "correct now-false self-instance claim in #27 dispatch doc". The PR replaced one now-false hand-written state claim with another now-false hand-written state claim, one commit apart, in the same file, and no prior reviewer saw it: the record at 7da6f47 (cloud-reviewer-clock-01N9VKEa.json) was filed before a147d1d existed.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. The sentence's conclusion ("this PR is not currently a live instance") is still TRUE -- a31f0ef also modifies HANDOFF.md and is also not record-only -- and I want that on the record, because it means the argument survives. But the clause "its green `lwb-lanes` does attest to review of `7da6f47`'s content" is now actively misleading: lwb-lanes at this head demands a record naming a31f0ef and rejects the two records naming 7da6f47 and bc6874c as STALE. An auditor following this sentence would look for the record that discharges the gate at 7da6f47, find one sitting there, and conclude the gate is satisfied when it is not.

EVIDENCE THE AUTHOR KNEW THE DURABLE FORM. The identical correction was made in the same commit to proof/43.json's criterion 4, and there it was written WITHOUT a sha: "re-deriving resolve_reviewable_head from this branch's tip resolves to a commit that modifies HANDOFF.md, not the base and not record-only." That sentence is still true today and will stay true. The markdown sibling got the hardcoded sha. This is the scoped-fix/unfixed-sibling shape this repository has shipped before.

FIX: delete the two `7da6f47` references and use the general form already present in proof/43.json. No sha, nothing to go stale, no re-review treadmill.

D2 (BLOCKING). proof/43.json's `commit` field names a superseded version of the deliverable.

`"commit": "e2d9f60"`. The semantics of this field were established on this branch by commit 23d742a, in its own message, in plain words: "`commit` corrected to `e2d9f60`, this branch's own current version of reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md (the deliverable this record proves)" -- i.e. the newest commit touching the deliverable file. That was correct when 23d742a was written.

MEASURED at this head:
    git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD -- reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md
      -> a147d1d, e2d9f60, b224d1b, df0de55
The newest commit touching the deliverable is a147d1d, not e2d9f60.

a147d1d edited reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md AND proof/43.json in the same commit, and left `commit` pointing at e2d9f60. So the record now certifies the PRE-correction version of the document -- the version that still carried the false "this pull request is itself an instance" claim that a147d1d exists to remove -- while criterion 4 of the same record describes the POST-correction version. The record contradicts itself about which text it proves.

I nearly mis-charged this one and am recording that per the honesty rule: my first reading was that `commit` should be the branch head, and that e2d9f60 was simply wrong by six commits. It is not -- 23d742a's body defines the field as the deliverable file's latest commit, which is a defensible reading of schema.json's "The commit SHA this proof record proves", and under that definition e2d9f60 was right when written. The charge is only that a147d1d broke the author's own definition and did not update the field it was already editing.

This is the same doctrine reviews/README.md applies to review records ("A record is bound to the commit it reviewed, not just the PR it reviewed it under"), applied to a proof record. Nothing enforces it for proof records -- scripts/lwb_check_proof.py only checks that `commit` matches ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ (line 152-154). I verified that: lwb_check_proof.py passes at this head with the stale value.

FIX: set `"commit": "a147d1d"`. If that in turn is falsified by a later content commit, the same discipline applies as for the HANDOFF generated block -- the record must be the last write, or the field must stop naming a sha.

RAISED, NOT CHARGED AGAINST THIS PR (all pre-existing on main; this PR does not touch these files):

R1. MY VERDICT CANNOT UNBLOCK THIS PR, AND NEITHER COULD AN AGREE. reviews/43/ holds two DISAGREE records (cloud-reviewer-b.json, cloud-reviewer-b-01TkEV63aRVApynnDLt6h8tw.json) and two STALE AGREE records (cloud-reviewer-clock-011D6Aeb.json at bc6874c, cloud-reviewer-clock-01N9VKEa.json at 7da6f47). A DISAGREE is a hard error in _review_ok, not an abstention, so it cannot be cleared by adding a record. Probe P7 confirms: even a fresh valid AGREE at the current reviewable head leaves lwb-lanes EXIT 1. Someone with write access has to resolve the two DISAGREE records before this PR can go green, whatever any reviewer files from here on. I have not touched any record that is not mine.

R2. scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py's first volatile pattern is defeated by this repository's own notation. The pattern (scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py:257-266) joins the ref to the verb with `[^.\n`]{0,30}?` -- a character class that EXCLUDES the backtick. So "main is at <sha>" is caught and "`main` is at <sha>" is not (P1/P2 above). HANDOFF.md writes the ref backticked throughout, including on the very line I probed. The module's own docstring says the SHA-label pattern "accepts optional backticks around the subject and the value", which is true of pattern 4 ("main SHA: <sha>") and not of pattern 1. The docstring also names "a wrong-but-stable claim ... a same-shape sha cited elsewhere in prose" as an accepted limitation, so the gate is honest about D1's class specifically. But the backtick hole is not a documented limitation; it is a hole, and it is the reason D1 could only ever be caught by a human or by a reviewer like me. Entirely main's, raised for whoever owns that file.

R3. scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check is a shape check only and does not verify the generated block's proof count against proof/ (P5). The operating guidance I was dispatched with asserts that a stale count "a required check goes red"; measured, it does not. I am recording the correction rather than repeating the premise. Consequence: the ordering discipline this branch follows so carefully ("regenerate LAST") is real discipline, not something CI enforces.

R4. HANDOFF.md contradicts itself about proof coverage, four lines apart. Item 1 says "`main`'s #34 has no proof/34.json (unexempted) -- gap open"; the generated block says "22/22 proven / (all proven; none outstanding)". Both are shipped by this PR, and the prose one is the honest one. The generator counts the records that EXIST and never asks whether one SHOULD exist, so it reports a clean bill of health for a question it did not ask -- the "I could not check" / "I checked and found nothing" collapse this repository names as its signature defect, sitting inside the document that names it. Pre-existing (main says "21/21 proven / (all proven; none outstanding)" with the same #34 gap open), so not charged here, but it will keep being shipped until the generated line distinguishes "every record validates" from "every landed deliverable has a record".

R5. The generated block's "Open PRs: (unavailable: no `gh` auth in this environment, or no open PRs)" collapses the same two states into one string, and it is wrong at this head in a way that matters: there ARE four open PRs (#40, #43, #44, #45), and `gh` with GH_TOKEN works in a cloud container -- I used it for every REST call in this review. Pre-existing on main. Same class as R4.
